variants.specifics: Brackenford townsfolk; shapes: rumour1 = quest rumour as a complaint (wolves, Ulric's bounty), rumour2 = general warning pointing at the barrow Urchins and the mill (Wenna's seal), rumour3 = ordinary brush-off

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: The wolves have been at Ulric's sheep again! The old man says he'll pay good gold to see them dead.

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: Keep a hand on your purse. Those Urchins from the barrow robbed the mill in broad daylight!

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: Can't stop, the ferry won't wait for me.

variants.specifics: Cave town of miners; shapes: rumour1 = ordinary complaint about the work, rumour2 = quest rumour as fear (Spiders in the lower gallery), rumour3 = tip about a paying job (the assayer's stolen magic lens)

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: Down in the dark from dawn to dusk, and they pay us in turnips!

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: The Foreman lost good men to the Spiders in the lower gallery. I'd not go down there for all the gold in the mountain.

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: Somebody stole the assayer's magic lens right off his bench. He'll pay well to have it back, I hear.

variants.specifics: Swamp hamlet on stilts; shapes: rumour1 = warning to the player (Wisps took the Elder's grandson, a rescue), rumour2 = ordinary comic complaint about the damp, rumour3 = tip about work (Maud the herb woman wants marsh-lily roots)

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: Don't follow the lights in the bog, stranger! The Wisps led the Elder's grandson off that way.

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: Damp, damp, damp! My bread's gone green again.

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: Old Maud the herb woman is paying for marsh-lily roots. Mind the leeches if you go picking.

variants.specifics: Castle town with a garrison; shapes: rumour1 = gossip about the great (Sir Aldric beaten by the Undead, the Captain wants help), rumour2 = scandal pointing at a fetch (the Quartermaster's enchanted shield), rumour3 = ordinary brush-off on the Duke's business

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: Sir Aldric rode out against the Undead and came back alone! The Captain is looking for braver souls now.

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: A thief got into the armoury and took the Quartermaster's enchanted shield. Imagine the shame of it.

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: Out of my way, I'm on the Duke's business!

variants.specifics: Lake village of fishermen; shapes: rumour1 = ordinary gossip (the Harbourmaster's fish story), rumour2 = worry pointing at the beast (something in the lake tearing nets), rumour3 = plain news of a theft (Tobin's magic lantern taken by rogues on the far shore)

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: The Harbourmaster swears he once caught a pike the size of a rowboat. Nobody believes a word of it.

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: My husband's nets came back torn to ribbons. Something huge lives in the lake now, I tell you!

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: Rogues on the far shore stole Tobin's magic lantern. Without it, he can't fish at night.

variants.specifics: Wizards' college town; shapes: rumour1 = alarm pointing at the main trouble (a Golem in the east wing, the Archivist), rumour2 = tip with a promise (Master Quill's spell book lost in the catacombs), rumour3 = ordinary odd humour (a lost toad that was a student)

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: A Golem smashed its way out of the workshop and into the east wing! The Archivist is in a terrible state.

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: Some student lost Master Quill's spell book in the catacombs. Find it and you'll be the toast of the College!

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: Hmmm. Have you seen a brown toad hopping about? He was my student. It's a long story.

variants.specifics: Frozen fort on a mountain pass; shapes: rumour1 = ordinary complaint about the post, rumour2 = plain statement pointing at the Troll on the high bridge, rumour3 = worry pointing at a rescue (a lost scout, the Captain)

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: Snow in the soup, snow in the bedroll... I hate this post!

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: That Troll on the high bridge ate our supply mule. Rations will be short this winter.

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: A scout went out after the lost sled and never came back. The Captain fears the worst.

variants.specifics: Lava-forge town of smiths; shapes: rumour1 = general warning (Imps out of the vents), rumour2 = ordinary gossip about the great (Master Durn the smith), rumour3 = a reward heard of (the Guildmaster's stolen gauntlets)

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: Stay clear of the vents after dark. The Imps come crawling out of them!

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: Master Durn is the finest smith in all the land! Lords come from across the sea for his blades.

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: The Guildmaster's enchanted gauntlets were stolen from the Hall. He'd give a good reward to see them again.

variants.specifics: Crossroads inn and its hamlet; shapes: rumour1 = a pointer to a person (Hulda at the inn wants the east road looked into), rumour2 = ordinary brush-off, rumour3 = fresh news of a beast (a great Bear wrecked a pedlar's cart on the south road)

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: Looking for work? Ask Hulda at the inn. She wants somebody to see what walks the east road at night.

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: Leave me be, I've a wheel to mend.

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: A pedlar came in raving last night. A great Bear tore his cart apart on the south road!

variants.specifics: Farming town troubled by Ogres; shapes: rumour1 = shouted news of a captive (Hobb's daughter, the Mayor), rumour2 = ordinary complaint about the weather, rumour3 = lament pointing at a fetch (the chapel's harvest bell)

rumour1.speaker: Townsman
rumour1.text: The Ogres carried off Hobb's daughter! The Mayor is beside himself.

rumour2.speaker: Townswoman
rumour2.text: Rain, rain and more rain. The barley's drowning in the field.

rumour3.speaker: Townsman
rumour3.text: The Ogres took the harvest bell from the chapel. No bell, no festival... What a disaster!
